audit.whatIsWrong: Five strings say Tumble grants invisibility from the start of the game: 'her tumble (Q) goes invisible', 'Tumble (Q) to invis and reposition', 'her tumble goes invis', 'her tumble (Q) goes invisible and condemn out-ranges everything', 'her invis and condemn punish every overcommit'.
audit.why: Tumble by itself is a plain reposition that empowers her next attack. The invisibility is granted by Final Hour (R) — 'Invisibility during Tumble' is listed in the ultimate, not the Q. So for the entire pre-6 lane the entry has Ambessa respecting a stealth that does not exist yet, which is exactly backwards: levels 1-5 are when she is most trackable and most punishable, and 6+ is when the tumble genuinely disappears. Tumble is also 6s at rank 1 falling to 2s at rank 5, and Final Hour shortens it further — those numbers are what 'punish a tumble on cooldown' needs to mean something.
audit.corrected: Tumble (Q), 6/5/4/3/2: a reposition that empowers her next attack. Invisibility during Tumble only exists while Final Hour (R) is active.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vayne.json — Q Tumble (autoReset, no stealth flag), R Final Hour 'Invisibility during Tumble', Q cd 6/5/4/3/2

audit.whatIsWrong: Condemn is the tracked, matchup-defining ability in the whole full layer, yet its cooldown is never given and the condition on its stun is never stated.
audit.why: Condemn is 20 seconds at rank 1 — one of the longest cooldowns Ambessa faces in top lane, and the single largest exploitable window in the matchup. More importantly the knockback only becomes a STUN if the target collides with terrain: in open lane it is a reposition, against a wall it is a stun plus bonus damage. 'Dash to avoid it' is therefore only half the answer; choosing where you stand decides what the ability even does, and a melee champion with three dashes can pick that ground. Neither fact appears anywhere.
audit.corrected: Condemn (E), 20/18/16/14/12, 550 range: knockback, and only a stun if terrain stops you. Fight in open lane and bait the 20s before you commit.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vayne.json — E Condemn 'If they collide with terrain, they are impaled, dealing bonus damage and stunning them', cd 20/18/16/14/12

audit.whatIsWrong: Six strings credit Public Execution with 'passive armor-pen plus healing' / 'flat armor-pen' / 'R passive healing' (spikes[1].text, spikes[2].text, whys[4], whys[5], mid, late).
audit.why: Riot's Public Execution text grants neither armour penetration nor healing — it is a 1250-range blink to the FARTHEST enemy champion in a chosen line, a suppress on arrival, then a slam for damage and a stun, on 130/115/100. The kit file's 'heal' flag on R is a tooltip-parsing misfire (see notes). Here the invented healing is directly load-bearing: content.late tells the player Vayne 'out-DPSes your R passive healing', which frames a sustain race Ambessa cannot enter. The real reason her level-6 window works is the blink range and the suppress landing through a kite she has no other answer to.
audit.corrected: Public Execution (R), 1250 range, 130/115/100: blink to the farthest champion in the chosen line, suppress on arrival, slam for damage and a stun.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json — R Public Execution description, range 1250, cd 130/115/100

audit.why: It gives Vayne move speed when moving TOWARD nearby enemy champions, and Final Hour increases that bonus. The consequence is asymmetric and counterintuitive for the Ambessa player: Vayne closes on you faster than she retreats from you, so the moment she turns to kite is the moment her speed advantage disappears. That is the beat to re-dash on, and 'she kites you' as written implies a speed edge in both directions.
audit.corrected: Night Hunter (P) speeds her toward you, not away — her step-up is fast, her retreat is not. Re-dash the instant she turns.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vayne.json — P Night Hunter 'gaining Move Speed when moving toward nearby enemy champions'; R Final Hour 'more bonus Move Speed from Night Hunter'

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart is inverted against its own text at three of seven stages. win[0] and phases[0].side say Ambessa wins Level 1 while whys[0] and spikes[0].text both open 'Vayne owns the opener'; win[6] and phases[6].side say Ambessa wins 2+ items while whys[6] and spikes[3].text say 'Vayne reclaims it'; the same split appears at Level 3. The ratings compound it — phases[0] reads side 'Ambessa' with rating 2/10.
audit.why: A side of 'Ambessa' printed above a rating of 2/10 and a paragraph explaining why Vayne wins is three different answers on one card. I did not flip it: chart edits apply atomically, they are mirrored against the Vayne page, and guessing a power shift is worse than leaving a visible inconsistency. The prose is the half I trust — it is bespoke, it matches the kit, and I kept it factually correct — so the fix is to bring win[] and phases[].side into line with it, which is a call for the user.
audit.corrected: By the kit maths: Vayne at Level 1 (550-range Condemn and ranged autos vs one energy-gated Cunning Sweep), Ambessa at Level 6, Vayne at 2+ items (percent-max-HP true damage). Needs a human decision — see questionsForUser.
sources: champ-data/content/ambessa.js — win[0]='Ambessa' vs whys[0] 'Vayne owns it'

edits.before: Vayne owns the opener — at level 1 you have only Cunning Sweep and you're energy-gated, while her tumble (Q) goes invisible and condemn (E) out-ranges everything you have. Don't walk into auto range to last-hit; farm with the outer edge of Cunning Sweep (it doubles on the rim) and eat a little poke rather than feed her Silver Bolts stacks. Once you hit 2-3 and your Q-into-Sundering-Slam plus Lacerate are online you can punish a tumble on cooldown, but the trade only pays off if you land E's near-total slow first — without it she kites out and condemns you when you overstay.
edits.after: Vayne owns the opener — at level 1 you have only Cunning Sweep and you're energy-gated, while Tumble resets her spacing every 6s and Condemn out-ranges everything you have. Don't walk into auto range to last-hit; farm with the outer edge of Cunning Sweep (it doubles on the rim) and eat a little poke rather than feed her Silver Bolts stacks. Once you hit 2-3 and your Q-into-Sundering-Slam plus Lacerate are online you can punish a spent Tumble, but the trade only pays off if you land E's near-total slow first — and stand off the wall, because Condemn only stuns you into terrain.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your weak window — cooldowns are longest here and a tumbling Vayne pokes and kites you while you farm toward 6. Then R flips it: Public Execution blinks you behind the farthest enemy in your chosen line, suppresses through her tumble and crashes her down for a stun, and its passive flat armor-pen plus healing-on-ability-damage makes the follow-up brutal. Bait her condemn before you commit, then R in, Lacerate to lock her with the near-total slow, and Cunning Sweep into Sundering Slam — chaining each cast into a Drakehound's Step empowered auto. Without R up, do not chase; her invis and condemn punish every overcommit.

Then R flips it: Public Execution blinks you 1250 behind the farthest enemy in your chosen line, suppresses her on arrival and crashes her down for a stun, and there is no kite that outruns a blink. Bait Condemn first — 20s at rank 1 — then R in, Lacerate to lock her with the near-total slow, and Cunning Sweep into Sundering Slam, chaining each cast into a Drakehound's Step empowered auto. Without R up, do not chase; Condemn punishes every overcommit, and it hurts most next to a wall.

edits.before: This is Vayne's game, not yours. Her Silver Bolts deal percent-max-HP true damage on every third hit, so the more you build the more she eats you — and Plated Steelcaps does nothing against true damage. Once she has two items she kites your Drakehound's Step dash chains, condemns you into a wall for the stun, and out-DPSes your R passive healing the moment Public Execution is on cooldown. Win this lane on your first-item Q spike and snowball the map; if it goes long, group and force fights where your R catches her out of position rather than ever trying to 1v1 a fed Vayne in an open lane.
edits.after: This is Vayne's game, not yours.
